title: Finite colimits and their preservation from coproducts and coequalizers
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be categories. Suppose $\mathcal C$ has finite coproducts [def-galois-finite-coproduct], including the initial object, and coequalizers: for every pair $a,b:A\rightrightarrows B$ there is a morphism $q:B\to Q$ with $q\circ a=q\circ b$ through which every equalizing map $h:B\to T$ factors uniquely. Then $\mathcal C$ has finite colimits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. For every functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserving finite coproducts and coequalizer diagrams, $F$ preserves all finite colimits (preservation in the sense of [def-galois-exact-functor]).
